findings.source_quote: σὺ δὲ ἀναγνωσῇ εἰς ταύτην τὴν πόλιν μετὰ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων τῶν προϊσταμένων τῆς ἐκκλησίας.
findings.issue: The lexical metadata lists a causative rendering as an alternative for ἀναγνωσῇ. The selected clause assigns the reading to Hermas himself, together with the elders; it does not say that he will arrange for someone else to read. The future middle form does not by itself support that change of agency. The chosen main-text rendering preserves the source, but this advertised alternative does not.
findings.suggested_revision: Remove this alternative and retain the already listed “you will read it.” Any proposal to retain a causative alternative needs passage-specific linguistic evidence and fresh review.

findings.source_quote: σὺ δὲ ἀναγνωσῇ εἰς ταύτην τὴν πόλιν μετὰ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων τῶν προϊσταμένων τῆς ἐκκλησίας.
findings.issue: The simplified edition independently preserves Hermas as the reader in its main text, but its lexical metadata offers an unsupported change of agency. Having something read can mean commissioning another reader, whereas the selected clause says that Hermas will read together with the elders. The middle morphology alone does not establish a causative alternative.
findings.suggested_revision: Remove this alternative and retain the already listed “you will read it.” Any replacement alternative must be reviewed against the selected Greek rather than inherited automatically from the standard edition.

summary: Both main texts cover all three source paragraphs faithfully, preserving the speakers, names, negations, first-created assertion, world-order claim, completion and disclosure roles, and distinct distribution tasks. Revision is needed only for the unsupported causative alternative in each edition’s lexical metadata. The witness notes are compatible with the supplied project reports and distinguish corrections, bracketed letters, conjecture, and mediated versional evidence. This review does not authenticate unseen manuscripts or editions, verify the supplied hashes, or certify exhaustive collation.
